investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the Kubernetes scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available, with 2 nodes showing insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" indicates the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is at capacity on those nodes, and preemption could not free slots ("No preemption victims found"). The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. As a result, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, the eval runner never receives a VM ID or a ready state, and all required evidence fields remain empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production user impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules changed or node labels were modified, the effective capacity would shrink even if kata.peerpods.io/vm quota was not fully consumed.

TERTIARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota set too low for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same extended resource, the quota may be correctly configured but undersized for current demand.

QUATERNARY — a node or daemonset managing kata.peerpods.io/vm advertisement went unhealthy, causing the resource to be reported as zero on one or both affinity-matching nodes, making the exhaustion appear worse than actual VM capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission controller issue should be investigated.

If a new remote-agent-create eval run succeeds immediately without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the node affinity/selector rules on the pod were recently changed to exclude the 4 non-matching nodes intentionally and those nodes previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the root cause would shift to a configuration change rather than resource exhaustion.
If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource advertisement daemonset is healthy and reporting correct capacity on all nodes, the cause is pure demand exceeding supply rather than a reporting fault.

If sibling checks for local-agent-create or other non-remote agent checks are also failing, the failure scope may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool and could indicate a wider cluster or API issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on affinity-matching nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct failure mode rather than a pod-stuck timeout.
Add an eval that monitors the count of Pending remote agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60s) to detect scheduling backlogs before they cause full eval timeouts.
Add a node-pool health eval that verifies at least N nodes matching the remote agent affinity/selector have non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity.
Add a cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods (from previous eval runs) are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots after the withCleanup() lifecycle completes.
Add a cross-check eval that compares remote-agent-create pass/fail status against local-agent-create to distinguish kata.peerpods.io/vm-specific failures from broader agent API or cluster failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the same eval run with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing and triggering the contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner cannot create a remote agent, so it never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an eval-layer signal of a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a scale-down, node failure, or resource leak), the entire remote-agent pool becomes unschedulable.

Tertiary — peer-pod provider quota or VM limit at the infrastructure layer: the kata peer-pod provider may have a hard quota on concurrent VMs that has been reached, surfacing as Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm at the node level.

Lower confidence — node affinity/selector rules were recently tightened or changed, reducing the eligible node pool from more than 2 to exactly 2 nodes, making the system more sensitive to capacity pressure. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this directly.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the Kubernetes scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available, with 2 nodes showing insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" indicates the extended resource quota for peer-pod VMs is at capacity on those nodes, and preemption could not free slots ("No preemption victims found"). The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. As a result, every remote agent pod is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable, the eval runner never receives a VM ID or a ready state, and all required evidence fields remain empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production user impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules changed or node labels were modified, the effective capacity would shrink even if kata.peerpods.io/vm quota was not fully consumed.

TERTIARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota set too low for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same extended resource, the quota may be correctly configured but undersized for current demand.

QUATERNARY — a node or daemonset managing kata.peerpods.io/vm advertisement went unhealthy, causing the resource to be reported as zero on one or both affinity-matching nodes, making the exhaustion appear worse than actual VM capacity.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the same eval run with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing and triggering the contract validation failure.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the runner cannot create a remote agent, so it never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an eval-layer signal of a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even candidates. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., due to a scale-down, node failure, or resource leak), the entire remote-agent pool becomes unschedulable.

Lower confidence — node affinity/selector rules were recently tightened or changed, reducing the eligible node pool from more than 2 to exactly 2 nodes, making the system more sensitive to capacity pressure. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this directly.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T13:13–13:18Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With zero viable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~136–151 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in production-api; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the VM slot resource is fully consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the eligible pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any VM slot exhaustion on those 2 nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus any live workloads, with no auto-scaling or preemption policy in place to recover.

Lower confidence — transient burst: a temporary spike in remote agent creation (e.g., from other eval runs or user activity) may have temporarily exhausted VM slots, which could self-resolve; however, all three sequential checks across ~5 minutes all failed with the same message, suggesting the exhaustion was sustained rather than transient.

Identify and terminate any leaked, stuck, or idle remote agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active use, to free capacity for new scheduling.

Investigate whether the node affinity/selector configuration intentionally excludes 4 of 6 nodes from remote agent scheduling, and if so, evaluate whether those nodes can be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required labels) to expand the schedulable pool.

Review cluster capacity planning for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource: if the 2 eligible nodes are routinely at capacity, consider increasing the VM slot limit, adding eligible nodes, or implementing a preemption policy for lower-priority pods.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any remediation to confirm recovery before closing the investigation.

Note: this is an eval-layer failure. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence. Confirm with the on-call team whether live remote agent provisioning requests are also failing before escalating as a user-facing incident.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling policy or quota issue would need investigation.

If the remote-agent-runtime eval passes on an immediate re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief burst of concurrent pod creation) rather than sustained exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on re-run, the failure is isolated to the runtime eval's pod submission rather than a cluster-wide VM slot exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec was recently changed to exclude 4 nodes that previously matched, the root cause would shift from VM exhaustion to a configuration regression — this would be evidenced by a recent change to the pod template or node labels not present in the current source discovery artifacts.
If a different error message (e.g., image pull failure, OOMKilled, or API auth error) appears on re-run, the scheduling exhaustion was a one-time condition and a different failure mode is now active.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity (allocatable vs. allocated) and alerts when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, so VM exhaustion is detected before pod scheduling fails.
Add a cluster-health eval that checks the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, alerting if the eligible node count drops below the expected value.

Add a Pending-pod sentinel eval that detects remote agent pods stuck in Pending state for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s), providing earlier signal than waiting for the full eval timeout.

Consider a pre-flight scheduling eval that submits a dry-run or low-priority canary pod to the remote-agent node pool and checks schedulability without consuming a full VM slot, enabling faster detection of capacity exhaustion.
